key_idea: 2018^2 = dx^2 + dy^2 has only 12 integer solutions ((+-2018,0),(0,+-2018),(+-1118,+-1680),(+-1680,+-1118)), so for each point just look up the 12 candidate neighbours.
sketch: Enumerate all integer offsets on the circle of radius 2018 by looping dx and testing whether 2018^2 - dx^2 is a perfect square. Pack each point as x<<32|y in a sorted array, and for every point and offset binary-search the shifted point; each pair is found twice, so halve the count. O(12 n log n). Pitfalls: coordinates go up to 2^31-1, so use 64-bit and reject shifted coordinates outside [0,2^31) before packing to avoid key collisions; do not forget the non-axis-aligned offsets (2018 = 2*1009 with 1009 = 15^2 + 28^2).
